thesis_summary.thesis: Copart operates a global salvage-vehicle auction platform: insurers assign total-loss vehicles; Copart stores them at yard networks and sells them via online bidding (VB3). **[Fact]** Revenue comes from seller fees, buyer fees, and ancillary services on units processed, plus interest on buyer float balances. **[Fact]** Q3 FY2026 (Apr 2026) revenue was $1.24 billion (+2.1% YoY) with diluted EPS $0.43; international growth offset US units down 4%. FY2025 operating income was $1.70 billion on ~$3.97 billion GAAP revenue. The model is capital-light after land is in place with minimal leverage.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: No dated payoff, but two parallel mispricing reads: (1) **transitory US volume** softness while international mix grows; (2) **GAAP book understates owned yard land** carried at decades-old historical cost while recent Copart purchases trade at **$150K–$800K+ per acre** depending on market. **[Inference]** At ~$33 the stock prices mid-cycle cash flow, not the embedded real-estate optionality Copart deliberately bought (>90% owned acreage per ESG letter).
